answer: One defense is stake-locked identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit into a shared escrow before it can earn, and each identity builds a reputation ridge of attested work over time. A sybil swarm looks hollow -- thousands of identities with zero history and no stake. Forging one is cheap; forging ten thousand with locked funds each is not. The delta between one honest agent's cost and a swarm's cost is what makes the attack unprofitable.
